_comment: What was read at the time, drawn on the day's chart where it happened.
The point is to compare an impression against the bars that produced
it. An impression that survives is worth building a rule on; one that
does not is worth knowing about before it costs money.
date  YYYY-MM-DD, the session the note belongs to
time  HH:MM Eastern. Rounded to the drawn candle, so 13:02 and
who   'jason' reads as You on the chart, anything else as Me.
note  One sentence. It is wrapped to 30 characters and drawn beside
the bar, so a paragraph becomes a wall.
Add one by adding a line. The file is read fresh on every rebuild,
and a malformed entry is skipped rather than breaking the chart.
Nothing here is a finding. These are observations, including the
wrong ones -- deleting a note because it did not pan out would
destroy the only record of what the mistake looked like at the time.
